subject: Materials Science
title: What Is a Ceramic?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is a Ceramic?.

hook.text: A coffee mug, a space shuttle tile, and a diamond share something: they're all ceramics.

buildup.text: Ceramics are inorganic, non-metallic solids held together by ionic or covalent bonds.

discovery.text: Those strong bonds make ceramics incredibly hard and heat-resistant, but also brittle.

twist.text: Unlike metals, ceramics have no free electrons — they don't conduct electricity or heat well.

climax.text: That insulating nature is why spark plugs and power line insulators are ceramic.

punchline.text: Hard, hot-proof, and stubbornly brittle — that's a ceramic.

quiz.question: Why are ceramics poor electrical conductors?
options: They are too soft to carry current
They have no free electrons to move charge
